title: Aunque llueva: concessive and conditional links
summary: Aunque with the indicative or the subjunctive, por mucho que and a pesar de, and the links that set conditions: a menos que, con tal de que, siempre que, en caso de que.
focus: Concessive and conditional conjunctions with the indicative and the subjunctive
content:
## Aunque: a fact or a possibility

**Aunque** takes either mood, and the mood changes the meaning:

- **aunque + indicative** = *although*: you state a fact as information. *Aunque llueve, salgo a correr.* (It is raining, but I'm going for a run.)
- **aunque + subjunctive** = *even if*: you don't know whether it will happen. *Aunque llueva, saldré a correr.* (Even if it rains, I'll go for a run.)
- **aunque + subjunctive** with a known fact = *even though, so what*: the fact is granted but changes nothing. *Aunque sea tu jefe, no tiene razón.* (He may be your boss, but he's wrong.)

**A pesar de que** (*even though, despite the fact that*) works exactly like **aunque**: *A pesar de que estaba enfermo, vino a la reunión.*

## Por mucho que and a pesar de

**Por mucho que** = *however much, no matter how much*. It usually takes the subjunctive, because no amount will help:

- *Por mucho que corras, no llegarás a tiempo.* (However fast you run, you won't make it.)
- With a noun it agrees: *por mucha paciencia que tengas* (however patient you are).

With the indicative it reports a real, repeated fact: *Por mucho que estudia, no aprueba.* (However much he studies, he doesn't pass.)

**A pesar de** without **que** takes a **noun** or an **infinitive**, never a conjugated verb:

- *A pesar del ruido, dormí bien.* (Despite the noise, I slept well.)
- *A pesar de estar cansada, terminó el informe.* (Despite being tired, she finished the report.)

## Conditions that need the subjunctive

These links set a condition that has not happened yet, so they **always** take the subjunctive:

| link | meaning | example |
|---|---|---|
| **a menos que** | unless | *No voy a menos que me invites.* |
| **a no ser que** | unless (a touch more formal) | *Llegaremos a las diez, a no ser que haya atasco.* |
| **con tal de que** | provided that, as long as | *Te ayudo con tal de que me invites a cenar.* |
| **en caso de que** | in case, if by any chance | *En caso de que no esté, deja un mensaje.* |

**Siempre que** has two meanings, and the mood tells them apart:

- **siempre que + indicative** = *whenever*: *Siempre que voy a Sevilla, como gazpacho.*
- **siempre que + subjunctive** = *provided that*: *Iré siempre que me paguéis el viaje.*

## The same links in the past

When the main verb is in a past tense or the conditional, the subjunctive after these links becomes the **imperfect subjunctive** (-ra or -se):

- *Dijo que vendría aunque lloviera.* (He said he'd come even if it rained.)
- *Me prestó el coche con tal de que se lo devolviera el lunes.* (She lent me the car provided I gave it back on Monday.)
- *Dejé una llave en caso de que llegaras antes.* (I left a key in case you got there first.)
- *No salíamos a menos que hiciera buen tiempo.* (We never went out unless the weather was good.)

Facts stay in the indicative: *Aunque hacía frío, salimos.* (Although it was cold, we went out.)

vocabulary.meaning: although (+ indicative) · even if, even though (+ subjunctive)
vocabulary.example: Aunque llueva mañana, iremos a la playa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Even if it rains tomorrow, we'll go to the beach.

vocabulary.meaning: even though, despite the fact that
vocabulary.example: A pesar de que estaba agotada, terminó el maratón.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Even though she was exhausted, she finished the marathon.

vocabulary.meaning: despite, in spite of (+ noun or infinitive)
vocabulary.example: A pesar del tráfico, llegamos a tiempo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Despite the traffic, we arrived on time.

vocabulary.meaning: however much, no matter how much
vocabulary.example: Por mucho que insistas, no voy a cambiar de opinión.
vocabulary.example_meaning: However much you insist, I'm not going to change my mind.

vocabulary.example: No te llamaré a menos que surja un problema.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I won't call you unless a problem comes up.

vocabulary.example: Saldremos a las ocho, a no ser que tengas otro plan.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We'll leave at eight, unless you have another plan.

vocabulary.meaning: provided that, as long as (+ subjunctive)
vocabulary.example: Te dejo la moto con tal de que conduzcas despacio.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'll lend you the motorbike as long as you ride slowly.

vocabulary.example: Puedes quedarte a dormir siempre que avises a tus padres.
vocabulary.example_meaning: You can stay over provided that you tell your parents.

vocabulary.meaning: in case, if by any chance (+ subjunctive)
vocabulary.example: En caso de que no funcione, llama al técnico.
vocabulary.example_meaning: In case it doesn't work, call the technician.

vocabulary.example: Aunque no llueva, me llevo el paraguas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Even if it doesn't rain, I'm taking the umbrella.

vocabulary.example: Entregaremos el proyecto dentro del plazo, a no ser que falte algún dato.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We'll hand in the project before the deadline, unless some data is missing.

vocabulary.example: Por mucho que estudió, no aprobó el examen de conducir.
vocabulary.example_meaning: However much he studied, he didn't pass the driving test.

vocabulary.example: Aunque insistió mucho, no lo dejaron entrar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Although he insisted a lot, they didn't let him in.

vocabulary.example: Aunque cueste mucho esfuerzo, vale la pena.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Even if it takes a lot of effort, it's worth it.

quiz.prompt: Nobody knows tomorrow's weather yet. Aunque ___ mañana, el partido se jugará.
quiz.explanation: A possibility you can't know yet takes aunque + present subjunctive (even if it rains). Lloviera belongs with a past or conditional main verb, and the conditional never follows aunque here.
hints: A possibility about the future takes the subjunctive.
The main verb (se jugará) is in the future, so use the present subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: You are telling a friend what happened: it really was raining. Aunque ___, salimos a pasear.
quiz.explanation: You report a fact as new information, so aunque takes the indicative: Aunque llovía, salimos (although it was raining). Llueva clashes with the past, and lloviera would treat the rain as a mere possibility.
hints: Is it a fact you are reporting, or a possibility?

quiz.prompt: Provided that you help me, I'll finish today: Termino hoy con tal de que me ___ (ayudar, tú).
quiz.explanation: Con tal de que always takes the subjunctive: con tal de que me ayudes.
hints: Con tal de que is always followed by the subjunctive.
Use the tú form of the present subjunctive of ayudar.

quiz.prompt: Whenever I go to Madrid, I visit my aunt: Siempre que ___ a Madrid, visito a mi tía.
quiz.explanation: A habit (whenever) takes siempre que + indicative: siempre que voy. With the subjunctive, siempre que means provided that.
hints: Whenever, as a habit, takes the indicative.

quiz.prompt: You can use my bike provided that you give it back to me tonight: Puedes usar mi bici siempre que me la ___ (devolver, tú) esta noche.
quiz.explanation: Here siempre que sets a condition (provided that), so it takes the subjunctive: siempre que me la devuelvas. Devolver changes o to ue.
hints: Provided that takes the subjunctive.
devolver changes o to ue in the stem.

quiz.prompt: No iré a la cena a menos que me ___ Carmen.
quiz.explanation: A menos que (unless) always takes the subjunctive: a menos que me invite Carmen.
hints: Unless always takes the subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: I left a key with the neighbour in case you lost yours: Dejé una llave a la vecina en caso de que ___ (perder, tú) la tuya.
quiz.explanation: En caso de que always takes the subjunctive, and after a past main verb (dejé) it is the imperfect subjunctive: perdieras or perdieses.
hints: The main verb is in the preterite.
For the imperfect subjunctive, change perdieron to perdiera.

quiz.prompt: She lent me the car provided that I gave it back on Monday: Me prestó el coche con tal de que se lo ___ (devolver, yo) el lunes.
quiz.explanation: Con tal de que takes the subjunctive; after the preterite prestó it moves to the imperfect subjunctive: devolviera (or devolviese).
hints: A past main verb takes the imperfect subjunctive.
Start from the ellos preterite, drop -ron, add -ra.

quiz.prompt: ___ la lluvia, el concierto empezó a su hora.
quiz.explanation: Before a noun (la lluvia) use a pesar de without que. A pesar de que and aunque need a conjugated verb after them.
hints: What follows: a noun or a whole clause?

quiz.prompt: However much you shout, I'm not opening the door: Por mucho que ___ (gritar, tú), no voy a abrir la puerta.
quiz.explanation: Por mucho que + subjunctive: no amount of shouting will change anything, so por mucho que grites. If the shouting is already a real, ongoing fact, the indicative (gritas) is also possible.
hints: No matter how much usually takes the subjunctive.
Use the tú form of the present subjunctive of gritar.

conversations.title: Planning the hike
conversations.scenario: Elena and Javier are planning a mountain hike for Saturday, but the forecast says it may rain.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Seguimos con la excursión del sábado? Dicen que puede llover.
lines.meaning: Are we still on for Saturday's hike? They say it may rain.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Aunque llueva, yo voy. Tengo un chubasquero nuevo.
lines.meaning: Even if it rains, I'm going. I've got a new raincoat.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Vale, pero no subimos al pico a menos que mejore el tiempo.
lines.meaning: OK, but we're not going up to the peak unless the weather improves.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Me parece bien, siempre que salgamos temprano.
lines.meaning: Fine by me, provided that we leave early.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Temprano? Siempre que quedamos temprano, llegas tarde.
lines.meaning: Early? Whenever we arrange to meet early, you turn up late.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: A pesar de lo que piensas, esta vez pondré tres alarmas.
lines.meaning: Despite what you think, this time I'll set three alarms.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Aunque pongas diez, te quedarás dormido igual.
lines.meaning: Even if you set ten, you'll oversleep anyway.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Bueno, yo llevo los bocadillos con tal de que tú lleves el café.
lines.meaning: Well, I'll bring the sandwiches as long as you bring the coffee.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Trato hecho. Y en caso de que haya tormenta, nos quedamos en el refugio.
lines.meaning: Deal. And in case there's a storm, we'll stay in the mountain hut.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Perfecto. La última vez, aunque hacía un frío horrible, lo pasamos genial.
lines.meaning: Perfect. Last time, even though it was horribly cold, we had a great time.

listening.text: Aunque llueva, saldremos a correr.
listening.meaning: Even if it rains, we'll go out running.

listening.text: Aunque es caro, este piso me encanta.
listening.meaning: Although it's expensive, I love this flat.

listening.text: Siempre que viene mi hermano, cenamos pizza.
listening.meaning: Whenever my brother comes, we have pizza for dinner.

listening.text: No firmo nada a menos que lo lea antes.
listening.meaning: I don't sign anything unless I read it first.
listening.note: A menos que always takes the subjunctive.

listening.text: Te dejo mis apuntes con tal de que me los devuelvas.
listening.meaning: I'll lend you my notes as long as you give them back to me.
listening.note: New word: los apuntes = the notes.

listening.text: Mis padres me dejaban salir siempre que volviera antes de las doce.
listening.meaning: My parents let me go out provided that I came back before twelve.
listening.note: Siempre que + imperfect subjunctive = provided that, in the past.

listening.text: A pesar del frío, los niños jugaron en el jardín toda la tarde.
listening.meaning: Despite the cold, the children played in the garden all afternoon.

listening.text: En caso de que necesites algo, mi vecina tiene una llave de casa.
listening.meaning: In case you need anything, my neighbour has a key to the house.
listening.note: New word: la vecina = the neighbour.

guide.section: Aunque: a fact or a possibility

guide.tip: Ask yourself: am I telling you a fact (indicative), or a possibility or a fact that changes nothing (subjunctive)?

guide.section: Por mucho que and a pesar de
The same links in the past

bites.title: Aunque: fact or maybe?
bites.rule: aunque + indicative states a fact (although it is raining). aunque + subjunctive means even if, or a fact that changes nothing.
bites.example: Aunque llueve, salgo. Aunque llueva, saldré.
bites.example_meaning: Although it's raining, I'm going out. Even if it rains, I'll go out.

bites.title: Unless, provided, in case
bites.rule: a menos que, a no ser que, con tal de que and en caso de que always take the subjunctive.
bites.example: No voy a menos que vengas tú.
bites.example_meaning: I'm not going unless you come.

bites.title: Siempre que, two meanings
bites.rule: siempre que + indicative = whenever (a habit). siempre que + subjunctive = provided that (a condition).
bites.example: Siempre que puedo, ayudo. Te dejo el coche siempre que lo cuides.
bites.example_meaning: Whenever I can, I help. I'll lend you the car provided you look after it.

bites.title: In the past
bites.rule: After a past or conditional main verb, the subjunctive moves to the imperfect: aunque lloviera, con tal de que viniera, en caso de que hiciera falta.
bites.example: Me ayudó con tal de que lo invitara a cenar.
bites.example_meaning: He helped me as long as I took him out to dinner.

sorts.title: Siempre que: whenever or provided that?

items.text: Siempre que llueve, se inunda el garaje.
Te lo cuento siempre que no se lo digas a nadie.
Siempre que viajo, pierdo algo.
Podéis usar la sala siempre que la dejéis limpia.
Siempre que la veo, me sonríe.
Acepto el puesto siempre que pueda trabajar desde casa.

sorts.why: The mood decides: a habit in the indicative means whenever; a condition in the subjunctive means provided that.

sorts.title: What comes after the link?

items.text: a menos que
con tal de que
en caso de que
a no ser que
aunque
siempre que
por mucho que
a pesar de

sorts.why: Conditions (unless, provided that, in case) always take the subjunctive; aunque, siempre que and por mucho que change meaning with the mood; a pesar de without que takes a noun or an infinitive.

spots.sentence: No iré a menos que me invitas.
spots.why: A menos que always takes the subjunctive.

spots.sentence: Te presto el libro con tal de que me lo devuelves pronto.
spots.why: Con tal de que always takes the subjunctive.

spots.sentence: Aunque la lluvia, jugamos el partido.
spots.why: Before a noun alone use a pesar de; aunque needs a verb.

spots.sentence: Me dejó su coche en caso de que lo necesito.
spots.why: En caso de que takes the subjunctive, and after the past dejó it is the imperfect subjunctive.

spots.sentence: Siempre que voy a la playa, me quemo, a menos que me pongo crema.
spots.why: Siempre que voy is a habit (whenever, indicative), but a menos que always takes the subjunctive.

builds.meaning: Even if it rains, we'll go to the concert.

builds.text: No salgo a menos que me llames.
builds.meaning: I'm not going out unless you call me.

builds.text: Firmaré con tal de que cambiéis esta cláusula.
builds.meaning: I'll sign provided that you change this clause.

builds.text: A pesar del frío, nadamos en el lago.
builds.meaning: Despite the cold, we swam in the lake.

builds.text: Me lo prestó con tal de que lo cuidara.
builds.meaning: He lent it to me provided that I looked after it.

realm.content:
## Aunque y con tal de que en Eldmark

Every deal in Eldmark depends on a condition. Risks and bargains take the subjunctive: **aunque el minotauro sea enorme, entraremos en la mazmorra**; **te doy parte del botín con tal de que me cubras**; **no abras el cofre a menos que la maga lo revise**. A fact you report takes the indicative: **aunque es tarde, seguimos**.

vocabulary.example: Aunque el minotauro sea enorme, entraremos en la mazmorra.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Even if the minotaur is huge, we'll go into the dungeon.

vocabulary.example: No abras el cofre a menos que la maga lo revise.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Don't open the chest unless the mage checks it.

vocabulary.example: El enano te vende el hacha con tal de que pagues en oro.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The dwarf will sell you the axe as long as you pay in gold.

vocabulary.example: Lleva pociones en caso de que nos embosquen los orcos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Bring potions in case the orcs ambush us.

vocabulary.example: A pesar de la nieve, cruzamos Frostmarch en dos días.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Despite the snow, we crossed Frostmarch in two days.

vocabulary.example: Siempre que volvemos de la mazmorra, lo celebramos en la posada.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Whenever we come back from the dungeon, we celebrate at the inn.

vocabulary.example: El cofre estaba vacío, a pesar de que el mapa decía lo contrario.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The chest was empty, even though the map said otherwise.

vocabulary.example: La maga nos dio una poción en caso de que nos hirieran.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The mage gave us a potion in case we got hurt.

vocabulary.example: Caímos en una emboscada a pesar de que el cazador nos avisó.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We fell into an ambush even though the hunter warned us.

bites.title: Pactos de Eldmark
bites.rule: Deals and dangers take the subjunctive: con tal de que pagues, en caso de que ataquen, a menos que llegue ayuda. A fact you report takes the indicative: aunque es tarde.
bites.example: Te sigo a la mazmorra con tal de que compartas el botín.
bites.example_meaning: I'll follow you into the dungeon as long as you share the loot.

listening.text: Aunque sea tarde, partimos.
listening.meaning: Even if it's late, we set off.

listening.text: A pesar de la nieve, llegamos a Frostmarch.
listening.meaning: Despite the snow, we reached Frostmarch.

listening.text: No ataques a menos que yo lo diga.
listening.meaning: Don't attack unless I say so.

listening.text: Siempre que vamos a Highgate, la elfa compra flechas.
listening.meaning: Whenever we go to Highgate, the elf buys arrows.
listening.note: New word: las flechas = the arrows.

listening.text: Esconde el cofre en caso de que vuelvan los orcos.
listening.meaning: Hide the chest in case the orcs come back.
listening.note: New word: el cofre = the chest.

builds.text: Te ayudo con tal de que compartas el botín.
builds.meaning: I'll help you as long as you share the loot.

builds.text: No entres a menos que llegue el paladín.
builds.meaning: Don't go in unless the paladin arrives.

spots.sentence: La maga vendrá a no ser que el gremio la necesita.
spots.why: A no ser que always takes the subjunctive.

spots.sentence: Nos dio una poción en caso de que nos atacan en el Bosque Umbrío.
spots.why: En caso de que takes the subjunctive; after the past dio, the imperfect subjunctive.

sorts.title: ¿Un hecho o una condición?

items.text: Aunque el orco es lento, pega fuerte.
Siempre que entramos en la mazmorra, perdemos algo.
A pesar de que llovía, cazamos en el bosque.
Te acompaño con tal de que lleves una antorcha.
En caso de que caiga el puente, cruzamos a nado.
No descansamos a menos que el paladín lo ordene.

sorts.why: A fact you report takes the indicative; conditions and possibilities (con tal de que, en caso de que, a menos que) take the subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: El enano forja tu espada con tal de que le ___ en oro.
quiz.explanation: Con tal de que always takes the subjunctive: con tal de que le pagues.
hints: A bargain's condition takes the subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: The mage gave us a map in case we got lost: La maga nos dio un mapa en caso de que nos ___ (perder, nosotros) en el Bosque Umbrío.
quiz.explanation: En caso de que takes the subjunctive; after the past dio it is the imperfect subjunctive, with an accent on the nosotros form: perdiéramos.
hints: A past main verb takes the imperfect subjunctive.
The nosotros form has an accent on the third-last syllable.

meadowbrook.content:
## Aunque y con tal de que en Meadowbrook

Farm life is full of ifs: **aunque llueva, hay que cosechar**; **Rosa te fía las semillas con tal de que le pagues en otoño**; **Leo no sale a pescar a menos que el río esté tranquilo**. A fact stays in the indicative: **aunque es invierno, la mina sigue abierta**.

vocabulary.example: Aunque llueva, hay que cosechar las calabazas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Even if it rains, the pumpkins have to be harvested.

vocabulary.example: Leo no sale a pescar a menos que el río esté tranquilo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Leo doesn't go fishing unless the river is calm.

vocabulary.example: Rosa me fía las semillas con tal de que le pague en otoño.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Rosa sells me the seeds on credit as long as I pay her in autumn.

vocabulary.example: Siempre que voy a la taberna, el alcalde me invita a algo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Whenever I go to the tavern, the mayor buys me something.

vocabulary.example: A pesar del calor, las fresas crecieron muy bien.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Despite the heat, the strawberries grew very well.

vocabulary.example: Guardo maíz en caso de que el invierno sea largo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm keeping corn in case the winter is long.

vocabulary.meaning: to sell on credit, to trust someone to pay later
vocabulary.example: En la tienda de Rosa te fían si eres de Meadowbrook.
vocabulary.example_meaning: At Rosa's shop they give you credit if you're from Meadowbrook.

vocabulary.example: A pesar de la tormenta, la cosecha fue buena.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Despite the storm, the harvest was good.

vocabulary.example: Cierra el gallinero aunque no veas al zorro.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Shut the hen house even if you don't see the fox.

bites.title: Ifs on the farm
bites.rule: Farm plans depend on conditions. These take the subjunctive: a menos que, con tal de que and en caso de que. With aunque, the subjunctive means even if.
bites.example: Aunque llueva, Nora planta el maíz.
bites.example_meaning: Even if it rains, Nora is planting the corn.

listening.text: Aunque nieve, abro la tienda.
listening.meaning: Even if it snows, I'm opening the shop.

listening.text: Leo pesca siempre que hace sol.
listening.meaning: Leo goes fishing whenever it's sunny.

listening.text: A pesar del frío, la cosecha fue buena.
listening.meaning: Despite the cold, the harvest was good.
listening.note: New word: la cosecha = the harvest.

listening.text: Iré al festival con tal de que bailes conmigo.
listening.meaning: I'll go to the festival as long as you dance with me.

listening.text: Cierra el gallinero en caso de que venga el zorro.
listening.meaning: Shut the hen house in case the fox comes.
listening.note: New word: el zorro = the fox.

builds.text: Aunque llueva, Nora cosechará las calabazas.
builds.meaning: Even if it rains, Nora will harvest the pumpkins.

builds.text: Rosa te fía con tal de que pagues.
builds.meaning: Rosa gives you credit as long as you pay.

spots.sentence: El alcalde abrirá el festival a menos que llueve.
spots.why: A menos que always takes the subjunctive.

spots.sentence: Rosa me dio las semillas con tal de que le pago en otoño.
spots.why: Con tal de que takes the subjunctive; after the past dio, the imperfect subjunctive.

sorts.title: Siempre que en la granja

items.text: Siempre que llueve, las vacas se quedan en el establo.
Siempre que Leo pesca un salmón, lo celebra en la taberna.
Te presto la barca siempre que la devuelvas antes de la noche.
Puedes coger fresas siempre que dejes algunas para el festival.

sorts.why: A habit in the indicative means whenever; a condition in the subjunctive means provided that.

quiz.prompt: Leo no sale a pescar a menos que el río ___ tranquilo.
quiz.explanation: A menos que always takes the subjunctive: a menos que el río esté tranquilo.
hints: Unless takes the subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: Whenever I go to the mine, I find something strange: Siempre que ___ (ir, yo) a la mina, encuentro algo raro.
quiz.explanation: A habit means whenever, so siempre que takes the indicative: siempre que voy.
hints: Whenever, as a habit, takes the indicative.

conversations.title: Seeds on credit
conversations.scenario: Nora wants pumpkin seeds at Rosa's shop but is short of money before the harvest.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Rosa, quiero plantar calabazas, aunque ahora no tengo mucho dinero.
lines.meaning: Rosa, I want to plant pumpkins, although I don't have much money right now.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: No pasa nada. Te las fío con tal de que me pagues después de la cosecha.
lines.meaning: No problem. I'll give you them on credit as long as you pay me after the harvest.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Y en caso de que la lluvia estropee la cosecha?
lines.meaning: And in case the rain ruins the harvest?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Aunque llueva mucho, las calabazas aguantan. Son muy duras.
lines.meaning: Even if it rains a lot, pumpkins hold up. They're very tough.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Vale. Las plantaré mañana, a menos que el alcalde me necesite para el festival.
lines.meaning: OK. I'll plant them tomorrow, unless the mayor needs me for the festival.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Siempre que vienes a la tienda, me alegras el día.
lines.meaning: Whenever you come to the shop, you brighten my day.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Qué amable! A pesar del trabajo, siempre tienes tiempo para charlar.
lines.meaning: How kind! Despite all the work, you always have time for a chat.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Para eso estamos los vecinos. ¡Suerte con las calabazas!
lines.meaning: That's what neighbours are for. Good luck with the pumpkins!

rustwake.content:
## Aunque y en caso de que en el páramo

Out in the wasteland nothing is certain: **aunque haya una tormenta de ceniza, saldremos a explorar**; **lleva el radiorreloj en caso de que te pierdas**; **el robot jardinero no funciona a menos que lo repares**. A fact you can see takes the indicative: **aunque hace sol, hay mucho polvo**.

vocabulary.example: Aunque haya polvo, Leo el buscador sale a explorar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Even if there's dust, Leo the scavenger goes out exploring.

vocabulary.example: Lleva el radiorreloj en caso de que te pierdas en el páramo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Take the wrist radio in case you get lost in the wasteland.

vocabulary.example: El robot jardinero no planta nada a menos que lo repares.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The robot gardener won't plant anything unless you repair it.

vocabulary.example: Marta te guarda la armadura con tal de que le pagues diez tuercas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Marta will keep your armour for you as long as you pay her ten nuts.

vocabulary.example: A pesar de la tormenta de ceniza, llegamos al mercado.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Despite the ash storm, we reached the market.

vocabulary.example: Por mucho que lo intentes, el capataz Ruiz no te dará más tuercas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: However hard you try, Foreman Ruiz won't give you more nuts.

vocabulary.example: Marta no acepta tuercas oxidadas, aunque se lo pidas por favor.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Marta doesn't accept rusty nuts, even if you ask her nicely.

vocabulary.example: No salgas de la cúpula en caso de que empiece la tormenta de ceniza.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Don't leave the Dome in case the ash storm starts.

bites.title: Planes en el páramo
bites.rule: In the wasteland, plans depend on conditions, and en caso de que, a menos que and con tal de que take the subjunctive. aunque + indicative states a fact.
bites.example: Lleva agua filtrada en caso de que no encuentres el pueblo.
bites.example_meaning: Take filtered water in case you don't find the town.

listening.text: Aunque hay polvo, exploramos.
listening.meaning: Although there's dust, we're exploring.

listening.text: No salgas a menos que pare la tormenta.
listening.meaning: Don't go out unless the storm stops.

listening.text: Marta acepta tuercas siempre que no estén oxidadas.
listening.meaning: Marta accepts nuts provided that they aren't rusty.

listening.text: Lleva gaseosa Zafiro en caso de que tengas sed.
listening.meaning: Take Zafiro soda in case you get thirsty.

listening.text: A pesar de la radiación, el robot jardinero sigue plantando.
listening.meaning: Despite the radiation, the robot gardener keeps planting.
listening.note: New word: la radiación = the radiation.

builds.text: Leo explora aunque haya tormenta de ceniza.
builds.meaning: Leo explores even if there's an ash storm.

builds.text: Te reparo el radiorreloj con tal de que pagues.
builds.meaning: I'll repair your wrist radio as long as you pay.

spots.sentence: No abras la puerta de la cúpula a menos que el capataz lo ordena.
spots.why: A menos que always takes the subjunctive.

spots.sentence: Ruiz me dio un tónico en caso de que me pongo enfermo.
spots.why: En caso de que takes the subjunctive; after the past dio, the imperfect subjunctive.

sorts.title: ¿Un hecho o una posibilidad en el páramo?

items.text: Aunque hace sol, llevo el mono azul.
Siempre que pasa la cabra del páramo, el perro guardián ladra.
A pesar de que caía ceniza, Marta abrió el mercado.
Aunque mañana haga sol, llevaré el mono azul.
En caso de que se rompa el radiorreloj, usa la antena.
Te doy tuercas con tal de que repares el robot.

sorts.why: A fact you see or report takes the indicative; an unknown future and any condition take the subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: Marta te cambia agua filtrada por tuercas con tal de que no ___ oxidadas.
quiz.explanation: Con tal de que always takes the subjunctive: con tal de que no estén oxidadas.
hints: A condition takes the subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: Leo said he would go exploring even if there was an ash storm: Leo dijo que saldría a explorar aunque ___ (haber) tormenta de ceniza.
quiz.explanation: Even if after a past main verb (dijo… saldría) takes the imperfect subjunctive: aunque hubiera (or hubiese) tormenta.
hints: Even if takes the subjunctive.
The main verbs are in the past and conditional, so use the imperfect subjunctive of haber.
